  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not
listed on the agenda but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be
taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each
speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Time may be surrendered by deferring (1) one minute to another speaker,
not to exceed a total of (8) eight minutes. The speaker wishing to defer time must be present when the item is
heard. In order to be recognized and present an item, each speaker must complete and submit to the Recording
Secretary a Request to Speak form prior to the beginning of the item being announced by the Chair (forms are
available at the entrance to the meeting room). Speakers are taken in the order slips are submitted.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting
where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public
discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning
decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of
the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is
desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may
indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to
adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission
following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public

speaker requests have been submitted.  Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral
Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting
with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral
Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall
follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are
on file in the Public Works Department, Malibu City Hall, 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, California and are
available for public inspection during regular office hours which are 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through
Thursday, and 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday. Written materials distributed to the Commission within 72 hours
of the Commission meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution (Government Code
Section 54957.5(b)(2). Copies of staff reports and written materials may be purchased for $0.10 per page.
Pursuant to State law, this agenda was posted at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the
deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance
with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please
contact Environmental Sustainability Director Yolanda Bundy, (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours
prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.
[28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

Requests for use of audio or video equipment during a Commission meeting should be directed to the Media Team
at (310) 456-2489, ext. 227, or media@malibucity.org. Materials must be submitted by 12:00 p.m. on the day of
the meeting.

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was

Subject:  Palisade Fire Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)
  Public Assistance Update

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive an update on the City’s efforts to apply for funding
for damages to public infrastructure through FEMA’s public assistance program as a result
of the Palisades Fire.

DISCUSSION: On January 8, 2025, a Major Disaster Declaration was issued for the
California wildfires, including the Pacific Palisades Fire (DR-4856-CA). This declaration
made federal disaster funding available to support response and recovery efforts for state,
tribal, and local governments including the City of Malibu.

The City has reported damage to public infrastructure that has been broken down into 16
projects with a total estimated costs of $12.4 million. Below is a list of those projects and
the anticipated costs the City may be able to recapture through FEMA’s public assistance
program.

  (Emergency Operations Center/Mutual Aid)

Subject:  Hazard Mitigation Grant Program Update

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive an update on the City’s efforts to submit Hazard
Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) competitive grant funding for projects as a result of the
Palisades Fire.

DISCUSSION: HMGP is a competitive grant program which provides funding to eligible
applicants so they can develop hazard mitigation plans and rebuild in a way that reduces,
or mitigates, future disaster losses in their communities.

The California Governor’s Office of Emergency Services (CalOES) responds to and aids
in recovery efforts following emergencies within the State of California. The Hazard
Mitigation Section supports mitigation efforts to reduce potential negative impacts of future
natural hazard events and disasters.

After the Palisades Fires, the City staff have been working with CalOES representatives
to develop a list of projects which can utilize this grant opportunity and enhance resilience
of the community.

HMGP project applications
Projects listed below were determined eligible activities under the HMGP program. City
staff have been working on grant applications for the following projects:

•  Codes and Standards
•  Telecommunication Undergrounding
•  Traffic Signal Backup Power
•  Big Rock Drive Slope Drainage
•  Private Property Wlidfire Mitigation

  Page 1 of 3
  Agenda Item # 4.B.
 Codes and Standards
The Codes and Standards hazard mitigation grant will include the funding to operate the
Fire Rebuild Center. This grant will cover the costs of the consultants, staff time and other
expenses to provide this service to the community.

Telecommunication Undergrounding Project
The Undergrounding mitigation grant will include the funding to underground the existing
telecommunication facilities serving the Big Rock, Las Flores/Rambla Pacifico, Rambla
Vista, and Carbon Mesa neighborhoods. Undergrounding these facilities, coordinated with
SCE’s ongoing undergrounding efforts will remove the existing wooden utility poles and
wires from these communities. The removal and relocation of these facilities will remove
the wooden poles and lines that could impact accessibility during natural disasters, reduce
debris and ember production along the roadway edges and may improve communication
facilities during evacuations and other natural disasters. The total project costs submitted
are $17,000,000. The City’s share of these costs will be $4,250,000.

Traffic Signal Backup Power
The Traffic Signal Backup Power mitigation grant will include the funding to install backup
power to the traffic signals on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH). Backup power systems will
be placed adjacent to the existing traffic signal controllers. If power is shut off to these
traffic signals, the new backup power system will automatically supply power to the signal.
It is estimated that this new system could supply between 32-52 hours beyond Caltrans’
existing battery backup system. This grant will cover the costs of the consultants, staff time
and the installation of materials to provide backup power to the traffic signals, specifically
during SCE Public Safety Power Shutoffs (PSPS). This project will improve safety on PCH
and will mitigate the hazards at these intersections during PSPS events. The total project
costs submitted are $600,000. The City’s share of these costs will be $150,000.

Big Rock Drive Slope Drainage
The Big Rock Drive Drainage Swale mitigation grant will include the funding to regrade
the existing drainage swale adjacent to Big Rock Drive and to install a combination of a
geosynthetic clay liner and a turf reinforcement mat within the drainage swale. These items
will help restore the drainage system along the hillside adjacent to Big Rock Drive. In
addition, these items will reduce the occurrence of surface runoff from entering into the
Big Rock headscarp. The Big Rock headscarp is the top portion of the Big Rock Mesa
landslide area and has a direct relationship with the groundwater levels. Preventing water
infiltration into the headscarp area is one way to maintain slope stability and to maintain
groundwater levels. The proposed geosynthetic clay liner and turn reinforcement mat are
effective methods of preventing surface runoff from infiltrating into the headscarp. The total
project costs submitted are $2,000,000. The City’s share of these costs will be $500,000.

Private Property Wildfire Mitigation
The City’s Fire Safety Liaisons currently provide Home Wildfire Assessments, which
provide recommendations in line with best practices for home hardening and defensible
space. However, full implementation of the recommendations can be cost-prohibitive for
some people. Therefore, staff is proposing that the City request $1,400,000 in HMGP

  Page 2 of 3
  Agenda Item # 4.B.
 funds with the City’s share of these costs will be $350,000 to implement a Home Hardening
and Defensible Space Rebate Program (Program) to help incentivize implementation of
these recommendations.

The Program would offer a 75% rebate to homeowners who complete qualifying home
hardening and defensible space projects. Eligible projects include, but are not limited to,
replacing roof, siding, and decking materials with non-combustible, ignition-resistant
materials, installing flame-resistant vents, removing flammable materials within the first
five feet around the home, and removing hazardous trees and shrubs. Rebates would be
capped at $10,000 for home hardening projects and $10,000 for defensible space projects.
Residents participating in both types of projects could be eligible for rebates totaling up to
$20,000.

On August 25, 2025 the City Council, Council authorized the funding match letter and
submission of the grant subapplication for Codes and Standards project. The remaining
four projects are scheduled for the September 8th City Council meeting for Council
authorization. The deadline for submitting applications to CalOES is September 15th.
